body.label: Bluefin trevally (Caranx melampygus)
body.info: A bluefin trevally: a fast, side-flattened oval with a steep forehead, sickle-shaped pectoral fins, tall front lobes on the soft dorsal and anal fins, a row of bony scutes along the rear of the lateral line, a very thin tail stalk and a deeply forked tail.

measured.counts: Dorsal spines (total): 9; Dorsal soft rays (total): 21 - 24; Anal spines : 3; Anal soft rays : 17 - 21; Vertebrae : 24. This species is distinguished by the following characters: gill rakers (including rudiments) 5-9 + 17-21 = 25-29 (usually 26-27); breast completely scaly; straight part of lateral line with 0-10 anterior scales followed by 27-42 strong scutes; adipose eyelid weakly developed, sma

caudal._origin_proc: uUp, uLo MEASURED on Camel_u3.jpg (FishBase painting) with the stalk writer's scale (flesh end at outline.tailEnd): the upper edge leaves the stalk at picture x 503, the lower at x 503 (where the fin's leading edge rises off the stalk outline); read by eye on a gridded crop at 3-10x, quality low, about +-2 px. The upper and lower edge leaves the stalk AT the flesh margin on this picture (no procurrent stretch visible): set to the margin's own end, so the reader tags the edge and grows no membrane. up, lo = 8 / 7 ESTIMATE (generic percomorph; not counted on a picture).

skin._origin_type: PUBLISHED FishBase (Caranx melampygus, Ref. 9894, 90102): juveniles and young adults 'head and body silvery grey', adults 'head and dorsal half of body brassy, suffused with blue' over a silvery lower half; photo skin_01 belly L* 90 with a mirror highlight (guanine).

teeth._origin: kind: an outer row of strong conical teeth with a band of small teeth inside (upper jaw); one row of conical teeth (lower jaw) (family description); counts and sizes are ESTIMATES

shape._origin_preop: h 0.5: Carangidae: margin smooth in adults, cheek scaled. ESTIMATE from the family diagnosis; NOT READ YET on this fish's photos

shade._origin: MEASURED, LOW: one strobe-lit live photo, plans/blueprints/images/trevally/skin/skin_01_side.jpg (iNat 21662572, CC BY) back 67.1 / belly 90.2; agrees with FishBase (adults: head and dorsal half brassy suffused with blue; silvery below). Not used: skin_02 (ambient, blue cast: 41.6 / 41.4). Method (Species, 16 Nov, plans/species_system/proposals/coat_fields/): L* = CIE L* (sRGB, D65) median of the pixels in boxes on the back third and the belly third of the flank at mid-body, a lightness (no length scale); look-and-measure only. Only strobe-lit live photos are used (ambient light from above darkens the belly; dead specimens change colour). LOW confidence: photo exposure and light direction move L* by 10-20, so treat |back_L - belly_L| under ~5 as no difference.

edge._origin_soft: ESTIMATE: the spots are too small to resolve on plans/blueprints/images/trevally/skin/skin_01 (dark specks, diameter 5 px) and skin_02 (blue flecks, 12 px), ramps at the photo's blur (upper bounds 0.86 and 0.64). FishBase: 'small blue black spots'; the blue flecks read softer than the dark specks by eye, so a little above the crisp marks (0.16-0.18).

How far the flesh runs past the hypural end (tailEnd - end = 4.0) is NOT measured: ESTIMATE, a side picture does not show the hypural end. rootHw ESTIMATE: a side view cannot show thickness; width / depth 0.57 at the stalk's thinnest station (u 169.7, measured depth 6.3), then a wedge: 72 % half way, 30 % at the flesh end, 15 % and 8 % on the fin. tail._origin_features: MEASURED on Camel_u3.jpg (FishBase painting) (side view, look-and-measure only; quality fair): u span on the flesh-end-at-tailEnd scale (apply_stalk_reads.py), y = height above the stalk's centre line as a share of its half depth at picture x 480 (+ up). n 34 = middle of the published 27-42 strong scutes (FishBase, Caranx melampygus): ESTIMATE until counted on a picture; h ESTIMATE.
